reasoning_traces.think:
The calibration pipeline operates as a dual-state system: first, it processes settled picks through a time hold-out split to maintain temporal integrity, then applies centered isotonic regression (CIR) to enforce monotonicity of predicted vs. actual outcomes. This calibrated output is evaluated using selected-slice ECE to detect potential paradoxes in high-value segments. Finally, fractional or portfolio Kelly sizing adjusts stake magnitude based on calibrated confidence and CLV deflation. The pipeline is gated by a compliance flag, preventing live deployment until adjustments are enabled. Failure modes include overfitting during CIR fitting, underrepresentation of +EV slices leading to misleading ECE, and insufficient CLV samples causing zero-stake deflation. Temporal consistency is paramount—random shuffling violates the pipeline's core assumption of temporal order preservation.
